title: Python SDK: Marshalling shims for typed streaming responses and graceful retry semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a compact set of "marshalling shims" in the Python SDK that: 1) accepts streaming chunks from the runtime and incrementally hydrates typed models (dataclasses or pydantic) without allocating full response buffers; 2) exposes a small ergonomic surface for developers to plug in retry/backpressure policies; 3) provides clear failure modes and recovery hooks for function-calling and structured-output flows. The goal is to make typed streaming easy and safe for common Redwood patterns (chat streaming, function call streaming, embedding streaming with retries).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end examples for dataclass and pydantic consumption of streaming responses (chat + function-calling) included in SDK docs and tests.
Streaming iterator yields partially-hydrated model instances (incremental fields) with deterministic ordering under backpressure and when retries occur.
Retry semantics: idempotent chunks are retried transparently up to configurable limits; non-idempotent transitions surface a clear 'resume token' and developer callback.
Benchmark: memory footprint for a 16KB/sec streaming chat session reduced by >=40% compared to naive buffer-then-parse approach across 95th percentile of messages.
Compatibility: existing high-level API (Client.stream(...)) remains backwards compatible; opt-in flag enables typed marshalling shims.
Integration tests for server-initiated resets, partial chunk loss, and multi-model fallback path succeed in CI.
Docs: migration guide and a cookbook (3 examples) added to docs site.
implementation_notes: Introduce TypedStreamAdapter: an async iterator that accepts a schema binder (dataclass or pydantic factory) and a small set of signals: CHUNK, FLUSH, RESET, END.
Binding layer has two modes: strict (fail fast on malformed fields) and tolerant (collect errors and attach to model.errors).

Retry controller sits between transport and adapter. It classifies chunks as 'idempotent' based on metadata (sequence id + deterministic rng seed). If classification unknown, mark as observable via callback.
KV-cache interaction: ensure adapter can rehydrate KV cache offsets when a retry includes a model-variant switch (e.g., quantized fallback). Provide lightweight API to re-apply cache slices.

Expose small public helpers: from_dataclass_stream(schema, *, strict=True), from_pydantic_stream(model_class, *, strict=False), and a StreamingPolicy object that accepts max_retries/backoff/total_timeout.
Keep default behavior unchanged: developers who don't opt in keep legacy streaming semantics. Flag is: Client.stream(typed=True, binder=...).
Avoid heavy runtime type introspection in hot path. Pre-compile small parse tables on binder construction to minimize per-chunk overhead.
tradeoffs: Strict mode offers stronger guarantees but increases developer-visible exceptions; tolerant mode is friendlier but may hide malformed data unless checked.
Adding retry classification metadata requires small additions to the runtime protocol; without them, SDK must conservatively treat many chunks as non-idempotent which increases surface for callbacks.
Pre-compiling parse tables increases startup cost on binder creation (minor) but reduces per-chunk overhead substantially (win for high-throughput streams).
Supporting both dataclasses and pydantic increases code surface area and test matrix; we prioritize common idioms but keep the core adapter extensible for third-party mappers.
test_plan: Unit tests: binder roundtrip for dataclass and pydantic, including optional fields and union types.
Integration tests: synthetic server that injects chunk drops, re-ordering, and resets; assert correct resume behavior and model stability.
Benchmark tests: memory and CPU profiles comparing naive buffer-then-parse vs typed streaming with parse tables on representative chat workloads.
E2E: playground example executed in CI that streams a function-calling conversation and asserts final hydrated model equals expected JSON across retries.
Chaos tests: run against Dedicated environment with induced network flaps and ensure adapter surfaces callback with resume_token for non-idempotent flows.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind python-sdk opt-in flag for the 2026-03 minor release (python-sdk-2026.03).
Dogfood in internal Redwood Console: integrate one chat demo flow and 2 customer-facing samples. Monitor memory/latency metrics for 2 weeks.
If no regressions, flip default to enabled for vNext with a migration note. If regressions seen, revert or limit to dedicated/premium tiers while we iterate.
Create 'migration-helper' script to scan codebases for callsites relying on buffer-then-parse assumptions and suggest updates.
